brief.headline: Ask for a price cut to ₹0.65–0.80/pc on caps and move to 15-day payment — they're profitable (keep 7.4% vs 5.0% peers) and carry an A+ rating, but sit in the grey distress zone, so pair the ask with supply security and a second-source plan.

priceAsk.summary: Target ₹0.65–0.80/pc on 28 mm induction-wad PP caps
priceAsk.basis: The open-market asking band for this cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc. The market verdict says MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec — our target sits at that lower end, justified by bundling volume and committing longer term.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days to 15 days after receipt in exchange for the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days earlier costs us ₹1.64 L in cash, but they borrow at about 7.02%, so paying early is worth roughly that rate to them — use it to sweeten the price ask.

brief.financialLeverage: PGP Glass is a big, stable player — ₹3373.51 Cr in sales, CARE A+ / Stable rating, keeps 7.4% profit (better than the 5.0% peers keep). But their Altman Z-score is 1.45, sitting in the grey distress zone, and they have EPF payment delays and pending legal cases. We're tiny to them — ₹39.99 L is just 0.01% of their revenue — so on our own we have almost no pull. The play is to bundle more volume, commit for a year or two, and qualify a robust second source (Manjushree or Mold-Tek) so they know we have a credible Plan B if they won't move.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate, nearly as big as PGP

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader in pails, containers, pharma — strong, profitable, robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging — broad capability across bottles and caps

brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to lock in a longer commitment at ₹0.65–0.80 per cap and move to 15-day payment — the market shows headroom at volume, you're keeping better margin than peers, and we're lining up Manjushree as a second source to de-risk supply.
